sentences: Randomness extractors turn weakly random inputs into nearly uniform bits, often for use as cryptographic keys.
Their guarantees must account for information an adversary already holds about the input.
The selected passage asks whether general seeded extractors with multiple output bits remain secure against quantum side information with suitable parameter losses.
The source contrasts this with more established one-bit guarantees and with specific multibit constructions already known to be quantum-proof.
Resolving the general question would determine how freely classical extractor designs can be reused when an adversary stores quantum information.
